description: A white pawn on a7 can promote by pushing to a8 or by taking the black knight on b8; each destination yields four legal moves, one per piece it can become, and counts once in mobility.
decisions: A pawn on its seventh rank reports promotion as available; its target is the first available promotion square in board order, the push square a8, even though the capture onto b8 is also a promotion.
Each promotion piece is its own legal move and its own lookahead entry, ordered knight, bishop, rook, queen; the side's legal move count counts all of them, as standard move generation does.
Mobility counts destination squares, so a pawn with a push promotion and a capture promotion has mobility 2 and eight legal moves.
The lookahead attacks of a promotion are those of the piece the pawn becomes, from the promotion square.

assertions.note: Eight promotions and five king moves.
The knight on b8 is attacked by the pawn and defended by nothing: the black king on e8 does not reach b8.
The queen on a8 reaches b8,  the knight,  and stops there; it reaches down the file to a1 and down the diagonal to h1.
The rook on b8 reaches along the rank to the black king on e8 and stops there.
Only the promoted rook or queen on a8 reaches a1 after a move; the white king cannot.
